data.title: Singapore targets $645m fund for SEA climate projects
data.description:
The programme will also feature a data platform and a market development facility.

Singapore has launched an initiative featuring a blended finance fund that will target up to nearly $643.5m (US$500m) to strengthen the climate resilience of SEA's agri-food systems.

Announced during the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, the Scaling Projects and Investments for Resilience in Asia (SPIRE) programme will bring together data, project development, and financing capabilities to help translate climate resilience needs into investable projects.

It was initiated in partnership with Temasek Trust, the philanthropic arm of Temasek Holdings.

SPIRE Asia will use catalytic capital to address specific investment risks and improve the risk-return profile for commercial investors, helping to mobilise commercial capital for projects and businesses that might otherwise struggle to secure financing at the scale or on the terms needed.

It is built on two other reinforcing pillars, including a data platform, which will integrate climate, agricultural, and investment data to identify climate risks and adaptation opportunities, inform project development and investment decisions, and measure resilience outcomes.

A key part of this effort is the solutions centre for regional smallholder farmers, which will develop a data insights platform to better understand the challenges in the region and help investors, researchers, project developers and solution providers develop and scale climate-resilient solutions.

The initiative will also feature a market development facility, which will work with partners to identify, develop, and aggregate agri-food adaptation opportunities into investment-ready projects.

The facility will provide technical expertise and project development support to help projects meet investors' requirements and connect them with potential investors, buyers, and implementation partners.

SPIRE Asia was jointly developed by the National Climate Change Secretariat, the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and Enterprise Singapore.

data.title: iWOW swings to $700,000 loss in H1 2027
data.description:
Datacomm revenue fell 41%, whilst wireless engineering declined 35%.

iWOW Technology Limited swung to a net loss of $700,000 in the first half (H1) of financial year 2027, partly due to lower contributions from its datacomm and enterprise solutions (DES) segment and wireless engineering solutions (WES) segments.

This compares with a net profit of $600,000 in H1 2026, according to the group’s financial report.

DES revenue fell 41%, whilst WES solutions declined 35%, with the latter affected by delays linked to a proposed consolidation of major telecommunications operators that was subsequently called off.

The group also attributed the net loss to a $500,000 reduction in grant income for its AgeTech innovation and higher factory rental and operating costs at The Gentle Group.

Delays in tender activities and project awards in the period further affected performance.

Revenue for the period also sank 12% year-on-year (YoY) to $16.8m, from $19.1m.

This was partly offset by growth in the group’s Internet of Things-as-a-Service, which grew 18%, and Smart City Solutions segments, which rose 86%.

The Gentle Group also contributed $2.3m to the revenue, following its acquisition on 1 July.

data.title: ComfortDelGro 9M net profit slides 20% to $141m
data.description:
Taxi and private-hire operating profit fell to $53.9m from $98.1m.

ComfortDelGro Corporation Ltd. reported a net profit attributable to shareholders of $141.1m for the first nine months of 2026, down 20% year-on-year (YoY) from $176.4m, partly due to weaker performance in its taxi and private-hire vehicle businesses.

The decline was also attributed to the absence of a $25.9m net gain from the sale of Victoria depots under the Zero Emission Bus Franchise contracts in 2025.

Operating profit fell 16.9% YoY to $235.2m, from $283.1m.

Meanwhile, revenue rose 4.9% YoY to $3.9b, from $3.8b, supported by growth in contracted public transport operations. Overseas markets accounted for 56.7% of total revenue.

By segment, taxi and private-hire revenue fell to $718.5m, from $778.2m, whilst public transport revenue increased to $2.62b, from $2.44b. Revenue from other private transport operations rose to $400.9m, from $356.1m.

In the third quarter, the group secured a contract for the Copenhagen Metro, with operations set to commence in September 2027.

It is also expanding its point-to-point transport business by growing its private-hire and partner fleets, as well as its premium and business-to-business customer base.

data.title: Central Region office rents up 0.8% in Q3 on premium demand
data.description:
Realion expects new supply to stay low until 2028.

Office rents in the Central Region continued to pick up in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, owing to robust demand for premium spaces, according to a report by Realion (OrangeTee & ETC) Research.

Realion said rents edged up 0.8% quarter-on-quarter in Q3, similar to the 0.8% rise in Q2, citing data from the Urban Redevelopment Authority.

Amongst properties the firm tracks, rents grew most in premium offices in Marina Bay and Raffles Place, both up 2.0% QoQ to $13.40 per square foot (psf) per month (pm) and $12.20 psf pm, respectively.

Overall office stock, meanwhile, fell by 72,000 square metres (sq m) to 8.1 million sq m, mainly due to the withdrawal of office space from the recently closed Harbourfront Centre and the 79 Anson redevelopment at Tanjong Pagar.

Island-wide office occupancy rose to 90.0%, with rates rising across the different regions.

In particular, occupancy of Downtown core offices rose to 90.5%, led by positive net absorption of 8,700 sq m.

Artificial intelligence (AI) firms led demand for premium downtown office spaces, with several firms in the process of inking deals, Realion said.

Occupancy in the Central Region outside the central business district (CBD) also increased, with the Orchard Planning Area and the Fringe Area rising to 95.4% and 91.0%, respectively.

With premium office space in the CBD becoming increasingly rare amidst growing rents, Realion said companies may increasingly look for well-maintained older Grade A offices, or explore alternative spaces in the city fringe and decentralised areas where rents are lower.

New office supply, especially in the CBD, is expected to remain low until 2028, with Newport Tower the only major office development expected to be completed in 2027.

Other major office projects such as One Comcentre, The Clifford, and The Skywaters, are set for completion in 2028.

The limited availability of existing office space, coupled with a relatively small pipeline of new supply in the near term, is expected to support continued rental growth, the firm added.

data.title: Genting Singapore net profit tumbles 42% to $55m in Q3 2026
data.description:
Gaming revenue dropped 22% to $315m on softer premium gaming activity.

Genting Singapore Ltd posted a net profit of $54.7m in the third quarter of 2026, down 42% year-on-year (YoY) from $94.6m.

Total revenue fell 13% to nearly $566.1m from $649.8m.

Revenue from the gaming segment dropped 22% to about $315m on softer premium gaming activity, consistent with a trend observed in key regional markets, Genting said.

The non-gaming segment, meanwhile, remained resilient, with revenue increasing 1% YoY to nearly $251m despite reduced hotel room inventory.

Adjusted EBITDA fell 27% to nearly $161.8m. On a normalised rolling-hold basis, it would have increased by approximately $36m.

Genting said Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) is strengthening its premium customer strategy by enhancing its business development and marketing capabilities.

The resort is entering the next phase of its renewal, including the upgrading and repositioning of its hotel portfolio, as well as enhancements to its gaming areas, lounges, dining, and guest spaces.

These works will temporarily constrain operating capacity through 2027, the group added.

data.title: Hongkong Land renames Wheelock Place as LANDMARK Orchard
data.description:
It is the first time the group has used the LANDMARK name outside HK.

Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd. has renamed Wheelock Place as LANDMARK Orchard, effective 12 November, following its acquisition of the property in August.

The office and retail property, which has been on Orchard Road for more than 30 years, was acquired by Hongkong Land’s Singapore Central Private Real Estate Fund (SCPREF). It is the fund’s first acquisition since it was established in February 2026.

The renaming marks the first use of the LANDMARK name outside Hong Kong.

LANDMARK sits at the centre of the group’s Central portfolio and is currently undergoing a major transformation through the more than $1.3b (US$1b) CENTRAL programme.

SCPREF has an initial portfolio of four premium commercial assets in the Marina Bay and Marina Centre districts: Asia Square Tower 1, Marina Bay Financial Centre Towers 1 & 2, One Raffles Quay, and One Raffles Link.

($1 = US$0.78)

data.title: Prime US REIT profit climbs 24% to $26.9m in Q3
data.description:
Distributable income also rose 27% to nearly $10.3m.

PRIME US REIT reported a net property income of $26.9m (US$20.9m) in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, up 24.4% year-on-year (YoY) from $21.6m (US$16.8m).

The REIT said the growth was driven by the commencement of previously signed leases.

Distributable income grew 27% YoY to nearly $10.3m (US$8m) from $8.1m (US$6.3m).

Q3 also marked the sixth consecutive quarterly increase in committed occupancy, which edged up to 84.2%, up 5.3 percentage points from its low of 78.9%.

Leasing volume stood at 131,000 square feet (sq ft), whilst rental reversion was negative 2.0%, compared with 6.2% in the previous quarter

The decline was mainly due to a 10-year early renewal with long-term tenant Holland & Hart for 68,000 sq ft at 222 Main, a 21-storey office building in Utah.

As at 30 September, 369,000 sq ft of signed leases had yet to commence, equivalent to 8.8% of committed net lettable area.

About 77,000 sq ft will commence in Q4, and 292,000 sq ft from 2027 onwards.

The REIT has extended the maturities of its $707.6m (US$550m) credit facilities and $86.2m (US$67m) loan to December 2026 while it completes a longer-term refinancing to replace the existing debt structure.

($1 = US$0.78)

data.title: CDL expects weaker performance in H2 2026
data.description:
Currency losses and possible impairments also add pressure.

City Developments Ltd (CDL) expects its financial performance in the second half (H2) of 2026 to be significantly weaker than a year earlier, it said in an operational update.

The caution comes after the group unveiled GET+ on 28 September, a three-year roadmap aimed at accelerating value creation.

CDL said H2 2025 benefited from a capital recycling gain of $473.1m on the divestment of mixed-use complex South Beach Consortium in September that year.

Citing persistent inflationary pressures and elevated interest rates, the group said certain capital recycling transactions originally planned for the remainder of financial year (FY) 2026 are now expected to be completed in FY 2027.

The anticipated weaker performance is further compounded by adverse foreign exchange movements, particularly the appreciation of the Korean won against the Singapore dollar (SGD) since July 2026.

The appreciation of the won has resulted in significant forex losses recognised by CDL’s Korean subsidiary on its SGD-denominated intercompany loan receivable.

CDL is also undertaking valuations of its property portfolio, which may give rise to impairment losses, it added.

The group said it remains committed to executing GET+, focusing on accelerating portfolio optimisation, capital recycling, and disciplined capital allocation.

It is targeting $6b in divestments by FY 2029 to crystallise embedded value and recycle capital from mature, non-core, or underperforming assets.

Proceeds will support balance sheet strengthening and debt reduction, whilst providing flexibility for selective value-accretive reinvestment.

In addition, CDL anticipates more than $6b of cash inflows from development sales over the next three years, as well as further cash inflows from its operating activities.

data.title: StarHub net profit nosedives 84% to $22.1m in Q3
data.description:
EBITDA also fell 26.3% YoY to $72.1m  on lower gross profit and higher opex.

Starhub's net profit plummeted nearly 84% to $3.9m in the third quarter of 2026, from $22.1m a year earlier.

The figure reflected the impact of high operating leverage as well as higher depreciation and amortisation, the telco said.

EBITDA also fell 26.3% year-on-year (YoY) to $72.1m from $97.8m on lower gross profit, higher operating expenses, and lower other income.

Meanwhile, total revenue rose 4.5% to $486.8m as service revenue increased 2.9% to $396.1m.

StarHub attributed the gains to an 18.4% YoY revenue growth in the enterprise segment.

Managed services led the growth, with revenue up 27.7% to $101.3m from $79.3m, driven by the delivery of projects and the timing of project recognition.

Carrier and voice revenue grew 10.1% to $32.8m, whilst enterprise connectivity revenue rose 5.2% to $38.4m.

The gains were partially offset by softer consumer segments, where service revenue fell to $223.7m from $239.2m

Mobile revenue dropped 6.0% to $121.2m as price competition weighed on subscription revenue.

Mobile average revenue per user (ARPU) fell to $19.2 from $21.7, whilst subscribers rose to 2.20 million from nearly 2.19 million.

Broadband revenue also declined 4.1% to $57.9m, with ARPU slipping to $31.9. Subscribers were broadly flat at 569,000.

Entertainment revenue fell 10.6% to $44.6m.

data.title: Private home prices rise 1.4% in Q3 despite slump in sales
data.description:
Resale volumes dipped 0.3% as the steepest drop hit developer projects.

Private home prices rose 1.4% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, faster than the 0.5% growth in the previous quarter and the eighth consecutive quarter of gains, according to data from the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA).

The overall price index reached 222.5, up 3.4% year-on-year (YoY).

Realion OrangeTee & ETC Research said in its Q3 2026 digest that the quarterly growth is the fastest in almost two years, since the 2.3% rise in the fourth quarter (Q4) of 2024, whilst prices rose 2.8% in the first three quarters of 2026.

Even as prices rose, sales fell 16.3% QoQ to 5,146 units in Q3 from 6,148 units in the second quarter (Q2), the lowest quarterly volume since Q2 2025, when 5,128 units were transacted.

Transactions fell across all sale types, with new sales posting the steepest quarterly decline at 44.7% and resale transactions dipping 0.3%.

The research firm attributed the decline to developers pausing launches during the lunar seventh month, whilst buyers held out for Q4 projects.

“The final quarter of 2026 will likely see a noticeable surge in transactions due to the highly anticipated line-up of a few blockbuster launches,” it said.

Lucerne Grand, Thomson Reserve, and The Serra will collectively add about 2,000 new private homes.

Thomson Reserve, specifically, is set to lift the overall price index in Q4 given its Rest of Central Region location. It has 1,268 units at an average launch price above $2,600 per square foot.

The research firm expects prices to rise 3.0% to 4.0% in 2026, with 21,000 to 22,500 units changing hands.

It said some buyers may exercise caution as interest rates could keep rising, after the US Federal Reserve raised rates in September for the first time since July 2023.

The Fed signalled that further tightening could follow if inflation stays elevated, Realion said, citing higher global import tariffs, an energy shock from the Middle East war and heavy capital spending on artificial intelligence.
